registry_info.name: sorting_hall
registry_info.description: Wave-1 synthesis (doc/plans/ARTIFACT_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md, backlog line 'initial_order sorting hall'). A SERIES built out of the ten bar_array_* tokens - one scene wearing ten names. Six sorts on one board, all handed the same array and all wound to the same fraction of their own work.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel synthesis builders never share one JSON. This artifact replaces none of its sources and must not be substituted for them: a bar_array you can stand in front of while it RUNS is the curriculum's spine, and nothing on this board moves. The hall is for a room that wants the comparison.

sorting_hall.name: Sorting Hall
sorting_hall.description: Six bar_array rows stacked on one board - bubble, insertion, selection, merge, quicksort, heap - every row handed the SAME starting array and then wound forward to the same FRACTION of its own total work and stopped. The rows are not drawings of the six algorithms: each one is bar_array_substrate.tscn with the source token's own lookup name stamped on it, so the family's cartridge, palette, region colours and highlights are the family's by construction. A work gauge stands beside each row - full height is the busiest row in the frame, the lit portion is what has been spent - counted in cells of the array rewritten, the one currency all six can be measured in from outside. `initial_order` sets what every row is given; `moment` decides which instant of the computation is standing in the room. Use #initial_order: and #moment:.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: footprint_cells is a COUNT, not a [w,d] pair - a pair crashes the placement engine. The board is 1.56 m wide, 2.25 m tall and 0.20 m deep, so it occupies 2 cells of floor and stands like a wall panel: wall_backing true, read from the front. Height is why the footprint triple carries a 3 while the cell count is 2 - the artifact is mostly vertical. Front clearance 2 because the whole exhibit is a COLUMN COMPARISON: the six rows are index-aligned and the reading only works from far enough back to see all six at once, which is about two metres.
spatial_needs.derived_from: board extent at array_size 32: 32 bars x 0.035 x 1.15 = 1.288 m row, plate 1.368, gauge column and margins to 1.556 wide; 6 rows at 0.36 pitch plus a 0.30 m bar = 2.10, plus margin = 2.25 tall.

sorting_hall.qfep_connection: Six procedures that agree completely about the destination and about nothing else. The hall is the clearest object this project has for the claim that a result does not contain its own history: the top and bottom of the axis - the given array and the sorted array - are IDENTICAL across all six rows, and everything that distinguishes an algorithm lives in a middle that is normally unphotographable. F_order is not one thing here; it is six different regimes of it standing at the same instant. Bubble sort grows its finished region from the right by exhausting neighbours, insertion by admitting one newcomer at a time on the left, selection by exhaustive survey and minimal displacement, merge by manufacturing sortedness in factory lots at doubling scales, quicksort by delegated local authority under a pivot no bar can see past, and heap sort through a tree that never exists as geometry. Same input, same output, six incompatible accounts of what ordering IS - and the work gauge underneath says they do not even cost the same kind of thing.
sorting_hall.relationships: Synthesised from [[bar_array]] and its nine named variants - [[bar_array_bubble_sort]], [[bar_array_insertion_sort]], [[bar_array_selection_sort]], [[bar_array_merge_sort]], [[bar_array_quicksort]], [[bar_array_heap_sort]], [[bar_array_histogram]], [[bar_array_fibonacci]], [[bar_array_prime_sieve]] - which are ONE SCENE WEARING TEN NAMES, the corpus's most common hidden family, and the reason the axis had to be declared ten times over after being written once. THE SOURCES ARE INSTANCED HERE, NOT IMITATED: each row is bar_array_substrate.tscn with the source token stamped as artifact_lookup_name before _ready, so the substrate's own _resolve_algorithm_from_lookup_name chooses the cartridge and every bar, colour and highlight belongs to the source. WHAT EACH ONE LEARNED, and what the hall exhibits. [[bar_array]] declares `algorithm` as its axis - the FAMILY IDENTITY - and its promotion note records why that is unsweepable on any one member: sweeping it photographs the siblings rather than the artifact. The hall is that axis laid out instead of swept, six of its nine values standing at once. [[bar_array_bubble_sort]] coined `initial_order` and found the one thing a still of a sort can honestly hold: not how far through it is, but what it was GIVEN. It also refused the family word `found_state` - sorted|stirred|mixed - because `reversed` sits at the same entropy rung as `sorted` while being the most expensive input the algorithm can be handed, and the whole lesson is that the cost model is inversion count and not disorder. The hall is where that refusal becomes an arithmetic rather than an argument: on `reversed` this row rewrites 992 cells and on `sorted` it rewrites none, and both inputs are perfectly ordered. [[bar_array_insertion_sort]] describes its sorted region as growing by ADMISSION and its O(n) best case as a quiet bias that rewards arrays which were nearly compliant already; standing it beside bubble sort at one moment shows the two O(n^2) sorts costing exactly the same and looking like mirror images, one finishing from the right and one from the left. [[bar_array_selection_sort]] calls itself a bureaucrat's economy - certainty bought at O(n^2) comparisons for the fewest possible swaps - and the work gauge is the first place in this corpus that claim is a quantity rather than a phrase: 32 cells moved against bubble's 992 on the same input, measured. [[bar_array_merge_sort]] says the array is never almost done, it is done at ever coarser scales, and at a matched moment its row is the only one showing sortedness at a SCALE rather than in a REGION. [[bar_array_quicksort]] says no bar ever sees the whole array, and its pivots in final position are the only structure on the board that is neither a prefix nor a suffix. [[bar_array_heap_sort]] imposes order through a structure the eye is never shown, and it delivers the hall's sharpest finding (see dna.finding): on `reversed` its build phase is FREE, because a descending array already satisfies the max-heap property at every node - the input that costs the two adjacency sorts everything costs heap sort nothing. AND THE THREE THAT ARE ABSENT, which is a credit and not an omission: [[bar_array_histogram]], [[bar_array_fibonacci]] and [[bar_array_prime_sieve]] carry `initial_order` because they share the script, and for them it is a deliberate no-op - the substrate's _arrange asks the cartridge get_category() != 'sorting' rather than checking a list of names, so a bin count, a Fibonacci series and a sieve cannot be overwritten by a ramp, and a tenth cartridge answers for itself. Only a sort is asked what state its input is in. That is why this hall has six rows and not nine, and it is the most careful thing in the source. Sibling in method to [[foresight_range]], the other wave-1 series, which holds four machines at one disclosure for the same reason this holds six algorithms at one moment.

dna.default: initial_order=reversed, moment=half - a free choice, because a synthesis has no shipped placements to preserve, and chosen to be the strongest single reading rather than the safest. reversed because it is the input on which the six rows disagree most: it is the worst case for both adjacency sorts (992 cells moved each, measured), the cheapest case selection sort has (32, one swap per opposed pair), and FREE for heap sort's build phase (0 of its 143), so one photograph carries the whole spread of the cost model - and every row still has work left to show at half. half because it is the only place the exhibit's claim lives - at start the six rows are identical because they have all been handed the same array, at done they are identical because they have all reached the same array, and the middle is the entire subject. Note what this default is NOT: it is not the family's default. Every placed bar_array ships at initial_order=shuffled, and the hall departs from it deliberately, because `shuffled` is the average case and average is exactly the case in which the six algorithms have the least to say to each other.
dna.was: synthesized from bar_array, bar_array_bubble_sort, bar_array_insertion_sort, bar_array_selection_sort, bar_array_merge_sort, bar_array_quicksort, bar_array_heap_sort, bar_array_histogram, bar_array_fibonacci, bar_array_prime_sieve. Nothing was refactored and no source changed; this is a new object built entirely out of instances of the old one. THE GAP IT FILLS is stated in the substrate's own promotion note and was left there as an impossibility: 'a sort is time-domain and a still catches one arbitrary pass, so how far through is not an honest axis for a photograph'. That is true of one row with a clock running - the moment is arbitrary because nobody chose it. It stops being true when the position is chosen deterministically and applied to six rows at once. The refused question is answerable here, and only here, because the answer is a COMPARISON and a comparison needs more than one body in the frame.
dna.axes_note: initial_order is REUSED CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER, in the family's order, and it is not retyped: the hall validates against ROW_SUBSTRATE.ORDERS, read at load out of bar_array_substrate.gd itself (const ROW_SUBSTRATE := preload(...)), which is the slot_machine pattern - eleven tokens now share the word and they cannot drift into eleven vocabularies. The literal @export_enum line is written out as well because the declaration gate reads the enum and GDScript cannot build one from a const; the two cannot disagree silently, since _pick validates against the preloaded list and anything it does not recognise falls back to the family's own default. THE SECOND WORD IS TAKEN AND ITS VALUE LIST IS REFUSED, on the record. `moment` belongs to [[laser_exploding_sphere]], which defines it exactly right for this artifact - 'the axis is not a parameter of the event but WHICH MOMENT OF THE EVENT IS STANDING IN THE ROOM' - and that is precisely what is being asked here. Its values intact|fissured|burst|scattered are the named states of a shattering and cannot be carried over: a sorting array has no fragments, no residue and no irreversibility, and inventing sort-flavoured synonyms for them would be the folding_past fault, taking a word without its answers. So the word is kept for the question it names and the ladder is this artifact's own: start|quarter|half|done, which names the METHOD - a matched fraction of each row's own total work - rather than a state, because the method is the only thing that makes the six comparable. This is the bouncing_ball precedent (took `regime`, refused under|critical|over) applied to a one-token word rather than a family one.
dna.the_unit: ONE CELL OF THE ARRAY REWRITTEN, and the choice is the exhibit's central methodological claim. Budgeting in cartridge STEPS was tried first and is wrong: the six steppers are not comparable and it is not their fault - heap sort's step() sifts an entire subtree, quicksort's does a whole Lomuto partition in one call, and bubble sort's compares one adjacent pair, so a step-matched hall would have reported heap sort at a tenth of bubble sort's cost, which is a fact about animation pacing wearing the costume of a fact about complexity. Counting COMPARISONS is not available either: the cartridges report comparisons in their step results, but merge sort's writes never appear in `swaps` and quicksort's inner Lomuto loop reports nothing at all, so the six would have been counted in six different fractions of their real work. So the hall never asks an algorithm how hard it is working. It reads the array after every step and counts how many cells hold a different value - measured from OUTSIDE, identically for all six, checkable against the picture by eye, and for the two adjacency sorts it is exactly twice the inversion count, which is the quantity [[bar_array_bubble_sort]]'s refusal of `found_state` was about. The array is always a permutation of distinct values, so 'moved' is exact float inequality and never a rounding question. WHAT THE CURRENCY CANNOT SEE, said plainly: it counts movement, not comparison. Selection sort compares O(n^2) times on every input and its gauge only shows the swaps, so on an already-sorted array its column reads zero while the algorithm is in fact doing its full quadratic survey. That is a real limitation of the measure and it is not hidden - it is the reason the row keeps its own magenta minimum-marker, which is the survey made visible where the gauge cannot show it. No single currency holds both halves of selection sort's argument; this one was chosen because it is the one the picture itself is drawn in.
dna.finding: MEASURED, not asserted, and one draft claim was wrong until it was. No Godot was run - captures are serialised centrally - so the six cartridge step() functions and the substrate's _arrange were ported to Python character for character and the per-step cell diff counted exactly as sorting_hall.gd counts it. Every number below is that port's output at array_size 32, and all six ports end sorted, which is the port's own check on itself. CELLS MOVED, whole run: on `reversed` bubble 992, insertion 992, selection 32, merge 160, quicksort 112, heap 143. On `sorted` bubble 0, insertion 0, selection 0, MERGE 0, quicksort 32, heap 193. FIRST FINDING, the one the gauge is for: bubble and insertion cost exactly the same on the worst input, to the cell, while selection - which the curriculum files under the same complexity class - moves 32, a factor of THIRTY-ONE less. That is [[bar_array_selection_sort]]'s 'fewest possible swaps' as a quantity instead of a phrase. SECOND, and the sharpest: a descending array already satisfies the max-heap property at every node, so heap sort's entire build phase moves ZERO cells on `reversed` (measured: 0 of its 143), while on `sorted` the build alone costs 44 and the run costs 193 - the single most expensive cell in the whole table. THE INPUT THAT RUINS BOTH ADJACENCY SORTS IS FREE FOR HEAP SORT, AND THE INPUT THAT COSTS THEM NOTHING IS HEAP SORT'S WORST. THIRD, the correction: the draft of this note said merge sort churns on an already-sorted array. It does not. Merge writes every cell at every level, but it writes back the value already there, so by the currency that counts CHANGED cells it moves 0 - four of the six rows stand still on `sorted` and only quicksort and heap move. FOURTH, visible only because the rows are side by side: at moment=half on `reversed`, bubble has 9 cells in FINAL position at the right end and insertion has 0 - its sorted prefix of roughly 23 is sorted but not final, being the largest values collected in ascending order, and every one of them still has to move. Both cartridges paint their region green. The two greens are not the same claim, and no single artifact could have shown that.
dna.measured: Port output, array_size 32, the two reproducible inputs (`shuffled` and `nearly_sorted` use Godot's RandomNumberGenerator and are not reproducible in Python, which is why no numeric claim is made about them). CELLS MOVED / CARTRIDGE STEPS. reversed: bubble 992/497, insertion 992/528, selection 32/528, merge 160/161, quicksort 112/127, heap 143/49. sorted: bubble 0/32, insertion 0/32, selection 0/528, merge 0/161, quicksort 32/126, heap 193/49. READ THE TWO COLUMNS AGAINST EACH OTHER and the choice of currency defends itself: heap sort takes 49 steps against bubble's 497 on the same input and moves 143 cells against 992, so a step-budgeted hall would have put the two at a ratio of 10:1 where the work is 7:1, and selection sort would have looked identical to bubble at 528 steps while moving a thirty-first as much. AT moment=half ON reversed, cells in final position: bubble 9 at the right end, insertion 0, selection 8 at each end at once (each swap fixes both), merge 0 at either end, quicksort 2 left and 4 right, heap 13 at the right. GAUGE HEIGHTS FOLLOW: at the default the tallest columns are the two adjacency sorts and the other four stand at 3, 11, 14 and 16 per cent of them. That spread is the exhibit and it is not rescaled to be tidy - a log axis would need a caption, and a caption is not a picture.
dna.declined: FOUR AXES REFUSED, each for a reason. (1) `found_state` - not relitigated. [[bar_array_bubble_sort]] refused it and the refusal is inherited whole; this hall is the object that proves the refusal was right, since `reversed` and `sorted` sit at the same rung of any disorder ladder and at opposite ends of every cost column on the board. (2) `algorithm` - the family identity, and [[bar_array]]'s own word. As an axis here it would mean removing rows, which is the AABB-collapse trap: fewer rows is a smaller box, the fixed camera re-fits to the union, and part of the measured bite would be the frame moving rather than the picture changing. It is also the exhibit's premise, and a premise that can be switched off is not a premise. (3) `comparison` - the six-token family word (single|fan|pairs|envelope and its cousins) names whether one instance or many are drawn, and this hall is permanently at 'many'. Its `single` value would render a worse copy of [[bar_array_bubble_sort]], which already exists, is already placed and is already promoted - a synthesis whose axis can degrade it into one of its own sources has forgotten what it is for. (4) An axis over the measuring stick itself - writes against comparisons against steps - which is the most tempting one here, because the choice of currency IS a claim (see dna.the_unit). It is refused as apparatus: an exhibit whose axis is its own instrument is the 'Reachability bench' question in doc/plans/ARTIFACT_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md, still awaiting a ruling on whether apparatus belongs on exhibit. Also declined: array_size (a count, not an argument, and every row must share it or the premise is gone) and step_interval (a rate, invisible to a still, and nothing here runs).
dna.framing_why: DERIVED, not guessed, and it lands on the same number as [[bar_array_bubble_sort]] for the same reason. Union box 1.556 x 2.25 x 0.20 m, diagonal 2.742, radius 1.371. The rig places the camera at dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so the visible half-extent at the subject is 1.9 x radius x framing - at framing 1.0 that is 2.61 m against a subject half-height of 1.125 and the board would sit in the middle of a mostly empty frame. At 0.55 the visible half-extent is 1.43 m: the board fills about 79 per cent of frame height and 44 per cent of width at the sweep's yaw of 0.62, for a subject share near 35 per cent. The projected half-diagonal is 1.29 against 1.43 of room, so nothing clips. The board is a flat panel, so the fit-by-diagonal penalty that costs a wide letterbox its frame is small here - stacking six letterboxes is what turns the family's 4.4:1 row into a 0.7:1 object.
dna.aabb_note: THE BOARD IS THE EXTENT ANCHOR AND IT IS REAL GEOMETRY. The bars are a MultiMeshInstance3D, which the capture AABB counts only when there is no MeshInstance3D content at all; the base plates and rims ARE MeshInstance3D, and they stop 0.30 m below the top row's tallest bar. A hall without a backing board would therefore have been framed to the plates and photographed with its top row cropped - the dna_specimen failure, arriving from the opposite direction. The board covers the true extent and not a millimetre more, and unlike a layers=0 anchor it does not overstate the footprint that sync_footprints.py writes, because a board this size is genuinely what stands in the room. It is also present at every value of both axes, so the box cannot move between variants and no part of a measured bite can be the camera.
dna.determinism: order_seed defaults to 20260805 - the substrate's own documented sweep pin - and NOT to 0, which is the shipped placement value. At 0 the substrate short-circuits _arrange and hands back the cartridge's own Fisher-Yates, which uses the global unseeded randi(): four variants would be four different arrays and any bite number would partly measure the RNG. That is the generative-artifact trap, and here it would be worse than usual, because the whole claim is that all six rows were handed the SAME array. There is no randf in this file, no _process, no timer, no physics body. Both winding passes are pure array work at build time. Two captures of one value are two photographs of one object, and no fixture is needed to make that true - which is why dna carries no fixture block: the hall builds complete in _ready with nothing gated on a player, a map or a controller, and both axes are String enums, so the typed-bool trap that cost the prompter's box a pass cannot occur.
dna.fixture_why: None, deliberately. The two things a fixture normally supplies here already hold without it: the seed is pinned by the export's own default (see dna.determinism), and nothing is gated - _ready builds all six rows, winds them and stops them unconditionally. auto_play is set false on every row BEFORE add_child, so no clock is left running behind the picture and the 1.1 s settle cannot advance a single step. Nothing needs to be handed to this artifact to photograph it.
dna.budget: Six substrate instances - 6 MultiMeshInstance3D at 32 bar instances each (192 total), 12 MeshInstance3D of plate and rim, 6 Label3D, 6 Area3D with one collision shape each - plus 18 gauge boxes, 1 board, so about 31 MeshInstance3D, 6 MultiMesh and 6 static areas. Two orders of magnitude under the ~3200 element budget. The winding is bounded by STEP_CAP 6000 per row against a true worst case near 530 steps at array_size 32, so a cartridge that never reports done cannot hang the build.
dna.still_note: Everything this artifact argues is standing geometry, which is the whole point of building it: the sources are animations and the hall is the still they cannot take of themselves. The rows do not move, the clock is off, and the difference between two values of either axis is entirely a difference in where the bars stand and which regions each cartridge has coloured. AN ALGORITHM THAT REWRITES NOTHING HAS NO MIDDLE, and this is visible rather than hidden: on `sorted`, FOUR of the six rows move zero cells - bubble, insertion, selection and merge, measured - so they stand at their start at every value of `moment` with empty gauge columns, while quicksort moves 32 beside them and heap sort moves 193, its worst input of the whole table. Two thirds of a sorting hall doing visibly nothing is the best case drawn instead of asserted, and it is also the honest consequence of the currency (see dna.the_unit). PREDICTED WEAK PAIR, stated before the sweep rather than after it: `sorted` against `nearly_sorted` at moment=start. At array_size 32 the substrate's _arrange applies int(32 * 0.12) = 3 adjacent transpositions, so six rows differ in about six bar positions each, by one thirty-second of full height - a couple of pixels at this framing. The axis's loud evidence is `reversed` against `sorted`, where every bar in every row differs and the six gauge columns invert; the critic takes the strongest pair, and the weak pair is a fact about how nearly `nearly_sorted` is sorted at n=32, not about the axis. WHAT NO STILL HERE CARRIES: the swap flash. The renderer bursts a bar to white for 0.375 s on every swap and the settle is 1.1 s, so the flashes are always dead before the shutter. The comparison and pivot highlights are target colours and survive; the flash never does. That is a real loss - the sources' liveliness is exactly what this exhibit trades away - and it is the reason all six sources stay placed and this replaces none of them.
dna.known_gap: No map places this yet, and the corpus's standing warning applies with full force: exactly one map anywhere places any artifact at a non-default axis value. A board whose entire subject is holding six algorithms at ONE chosen moment is worth nothing until somebody writes sorting_hall#moment:quarter or sorting_hall#initial_order:sorted into a map and stands in front of it. The obvious home is a datastructures room that already places two or three of the six rows individually, so the hall reads as the summary of things the player has met rather than as a poster of things they have not.
dna.trap_avoided: A PACKED ARRAY IN GODOT 4 IS PASSED AND ASSIGNED BY REFERENCE, and this artifact's whole measurement is a diff between two snapshots of one. The first draft read the row's array with Object.get('_array') and kept the previous read as `prev` - but the cartridges mutate the buffer in place (step() writes into the array it was handed and returns the same object, and the substrate assigns it back), so `prev` and `cur` were one object, every diff would have been zero, every total zero, all six gauges empty and every value of `moment` would have shown the untouched input. It would have rendered as a clean, finished-looking exhibit of an axis that does nothing - the exact shape of the six-ways-null table in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md, self-inflicted, and with no fingerprint distinguishing it from a genuine null. _read_array therefore returns arr.duplicate() and says why at the call site. Worth stating generally: any artifact that measures a source by watching its state across time must copy the state, and Godot 4 changed the default from copy to reference exactly where it hurts.
dna.harness_note: FOUND WHILE BUILDING, and it belongs to the family rather than to this artifact: the BasePlate and Rim BoxMesh sub-resources in bar_array_substrate.tscn are not resource_local_to_scene, so every instance of that scene in one scene tree shares one mesh, and _update_base_plate writes its size. Six rows at one array_size is safe and this hall is safe. Two bar_arrays at different array_size in one map are not - the last one to build sizes both plates. Nobody has hit it because array_size is left at 32 almost everywhere. Reported, not patched: touching a scene ten tokens depend on is its own change with its own test.
